errors.english: Lord, given that no phenomenon is apprehended when they have stood in suchness and practiced for suchness, how will they stand in the knowledge of all aspects?
errors.why: The commentary cites only the abbreviated lemma 'having stood in suchness and exerted oneself in suchness'; the clauses about non-apprehension and standing in the knowledge of all aspects are supplied from the sūtra, not this side.

errors.english: Lord, given that no dharma called 'a tathāgata's magical creation' is apprehended at all, who will stand in suchness?
errors.why: The Tibetan lemma is only 'Lord, that which is called a tathāgata's emanation'; the rest of the question is not on this side.

note: Accurate numbered list of the questions; two lemmas are expanded with sūtra material absent from the Tibetan.

errors.english: the ten perfections such as excellent rebirth
errors.why: phun sum tshogs pa here is 'excellence' (sampad), ten excellences beginning with excellent family, not 'perfections', which a reader will take as pāramitās.

fix.find: the ten perfections such as excellent rebirth
fix.replace: the ten excellences such as excellent family

note: Sound rendering of the benefits list and the gloss on remaining near; some unmarked explanatory glosses are inserted after śrāvaka/pratyekabuddha.
Faithful rendering of the Hevajra commentary on the joys, initiations and the channels lalanā/rasanā.

errors.english: by this Queen of Secret Mantras, the Retainer of Secret Mantras
errors.why: rig sngags kyi rgyal mo is 'Queen of Vidyās / knowledge-mantras' (vidyārājñī), distinct from gsang sngags; the English collapses the two.

note: Reliable rendering of the Mahāpratisarā ritual commentary; one epithet blurred.

errors.english: With her right red leg extended, the Consort is yellow
errors.why: The red extended right leg (with the white left of the previous side) belongs to the description of the principal deity; the consort's description begins with 'the Mother is yellow'.

errors.english: transformed into the deities of the stupa
errors.why: The beings become the maṇḍala deities (dkyil 'khor lha); there is no stūpa.

fix.find: transformed into the deities of the stupa
fix.replace: transformed into the deities of the mandala

errors.english: I abide as the personhood of the yogi
errors.why: In the series concordant cause / maturation / skyes bu / stainless, skyes bu refers to the puruṣakāra (person-made) result, not 'personhood'.

note: Usable Kālacakra sādhana translation, but iconography is misattributed at the side boundary and a mandala is turned into a stupa.

errors.english: is not the defining characteristic of the meditative absorption of yoga
errors.why: The Tibetan affirms that the samādhi of single recollection is the characteristic of the yoga samādhi that is a branch of the first application; no negation is present.

fix.find: is not the defining characteristic of the meditative absorption of yoga
fix.replace: is the defining characteristic of the meditative absorption of yoga

note: Otherwise a careful rendering of the generation-stage sequence; one inserted negation reverses the opening definition.
Faithful rendering of the Guhyasamāja commentary on the mantra of body, speech and mind.

errors.english: From a verbal root that involves (ngayik) movement or a specific grammatical marker, and is marked as (ngit)
errors.why: nga yig 'gro ba gang yin pa defines a ṅit root as one to which the letter ṅa is attached ('gro ba = 'goes to'); it is not a root meaning movement.

fix.find: From a verbal root that involves (ngayik) movement or a specific grammatical marker, and is marked as (ngit)
fix.replace: A verbal root to which the letter (nga) is attached is (ngit); from such a root

errors.english: (ngit) a marker indicating a specific class of verbal endings
errors.why: ṅit designates a root bearing the indicatory ṅ (which takes ātmanepada endings), not a marker of a class of endings.
The example of the rule is the ātmanepada form vyatilunate; giving the parasmaipada form undoes the point of the rule (and conflates it with the later counter-examples).

note: Paradigms and the parasmaipada/ātmanepada terminology are right, but the definition of ṅit is misread and the reciprocal-action examples are muddled.
Faithful rendering of the commentary on the applications of mindfulness as concordant with the perfections.
Faithful rendering of the Abhidharma commentary on dharma-pravicaya as the sole means; inline unmarked glosses are harmless.
